headline: Dakshina Kannada struggles with 20 severely malnourished children and over 8,000 anaemic students despite nutrition programmes
summary: Despite being considered a progressive district, Dakshina Kannada faces persistent child undernutrition challenges. Officials identified 20 severely malnourished children requiring urgent admission to Nutrition Rehabilitation Centres, with 41 total acute malnutrition cases reported. Over 8,021 children suffer from anaemia, including 268 severe cases, with government school students showing higher rates. The district lags in implementing supplementary nutrition programmes. Child marriage persists despite prevention efforts, with five cases thwarted in 2017. Approximately 149,400 children receive nutritious food through 1,494 anganwadi centres, alongside 13,380 pregnant and 13,793 lactating women.

modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Early marriage compromises maternal health, education, and reproductive maturity, leading to poor pregnancy outcomes and child undernutrition.

modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Early childhood education attendance correlates with better nutritional monitoring, parental health awareness, and regular access to supplementary nutrition.

modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Adequate maternal iron-folic acid intake prevents maternal anaemia, supports fetal development, and reduces low birth weight and stunting risk.
